evidence: Ticket 8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8 comment: 'Superseded by epic 119f-63e3-34b7-4f96 (shy-fussy-hermitcrab)… Closing as superseded (no code delivered under this id).'

Runtime seam infrastructure (CodeReviewBatchRunner fan-in, effective_criteria, _run_code_review_case, code_review_decide with effective_routing) IS verified present in the repo by grep — delivered by the superseding epic 119f-63e3-34b7-4f96, which is unlisted in the plan's dependency section.
findings.finding: The plan asserts 'child bug `8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8` owns the concrete repair' of the integration seam, but that ticket is closed with the comment 'no code delivered under this id — superseded by epic `119f-63e3-34b7-4f96`'. The cited-prerequisite escape (rebar:2c14-fa5f-1228-4e02) cannot be confirmed because the child ticket's own record states no code was delivered, so C's plan/file_impact does not establish the specific relied-upon functionality through that ticket. The seam code IS present in the repo (delivered by the unlisted superseding epic), so the capability is available — but the plan's dependency citation points to a ticket whose child explicitly did not deliver the work, leaving the claim 'depends on… whose child bug owns the concrete repair' without a valid citation path.
findings.location: Dependency section: 'Depends on the linked integration-seam story `2c14-fa5f-1228-4e02`, whose child bug `8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8` owns the concrete repair.'
scenarios: A reviewer or gating system trying to verify the dependency chain finds that the cited prerequisite tickets were closed without delivering code, creating a broken dependency audit trail.
If the superseding epic 119f-63e3-34b7-4f96 is later reverted or its delivery is disputed, there is no valid citation path from this story to the actual delivering work.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the AC #5 docs verify step (or a companion pytest assertion) to check that `docs/llm-framework.md` contains at least the four described elements (project-owned placement, phase contract, advisory posture, and eval corpus) beyond just the subsection heading.
evidence: Plan body: 'Add a `Project dogfood: review-phase-boundaries` subsection to `docs/llm-framework.md` explaining the project-owned placement, phase contract, advisory posture, and eval corpus.'
AC #5 verify: `assert "Project dogfood: review-phase-boundaries" in s` — checks only heading presence, not the four described content elements.
findings.finding: The AC for `docs/llm-framework.md` only asserts the presence of the heading string 'Project dogfood: review-phase-boundaries', but the plan body describes four distinct content requirements for that subsection ('project-owned placement, phase contract, advisory posture, and eval corpus'). An implementer could satisfy the AC with a one-line heading and an empty body.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC #5 verify step; Scope section ('Add a `Project dogfood: review-phase-boundaries` subsection…')
scenarios: An implementer adds a placeholder heading with no substantive content, passes the AC check, and the four described explanatory elements are never written.
findings.suggested_fix: Add four additional `assert` probes in the verify snippet or a parameterized pytest check, e.g. `for phrase in ['project-owned', 'phase contract', 'advisory posture', 'eval corpus']: assert phrase in s, phrase`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `outputs: code_review_findings` to the required front-matter fields in the AC for `.rebar/prompts/code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries.md`, alongside the already-required `execution_mode: single_turn`.
evidence: `_run_code_review_case`: `output_schema=prompt.outputs if isinstance(prompt.outputs, str) else None` — `eval_solver.py:240`
Every existing code-review overlay prompt declares `outputs: code_review_findings` in front-matter (e.g. `code-review-security.md:7`, `code-review-tests.md:7`)
AC checks `execution_mode: single_turn` in the prompt file but never checks for `outputs: code_review_findings`
Plan says 'declares `execution_mode: single_turn`' — no mention of the `outputs:` field
findings.finding: The plan never specifies the `outputs:` front-matter field required in the new prompt file. `_run_code_review_case` wires `output_schema=prompt.outputs` to select the Pydantic model that enforces the `code_review_findings` contract at inference time. Without `outputs: code_review_findings` in the prompt's YAML front-matter, `prompt.outputs` is `None`, the `RunRequest` carries `output_schema=None`, and the runner emits unstructured text — so the `{findings:[...]}` shape is never enforced by the model-binding layer.
scenarios: Author omits `outputs: code_review_findings` from the prompt front-matter (following plan AC literally); the runner receives `output_schema=None` and the LLM returns free-form text; the scorer's `isinstance(out.get('findings'), list)` check fails; the live eval returns all-false and the operator-attested AC cannot be satisfied.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the AC verification command to also assert `'outputs: code_review_findings' in s`, e.g.: `assert 'execution_mode: single_turn' in s and 'outputs: code_review_findings' in s`

Leaf ticket deps graph correctly records `41e2-a0a2-2db4-4847` as a dependency, but the plan text contradicts this by naming the superseded tickets instead.
findings.finding: The leaf's Dependency section names `2c14-fa5f-1228-4e02` (the integration-seam story) and its child bug `8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8` as the blocking prerequisites for 225a, but the parent epic (119f) explicitly supersedes both tickets, closing them, and instead designates `41e2-a0a2-2db4-4847` (seam child #5, CLI admission) as the correct prerequisite for 225a. The leaf's plan text references superseded vehicles rather than the parent-specified dependency.
findings.location: Leaf plan § Dependency; parent plan § Decomposition 'Feature children' item 7
scenarios: A developer reading the leaf's plan text follows the dependency chain to `2c14` and `8a4b`, finds them closed/superseded, and is confused about what seam work must land before 225a can be implemented.
Automated dependency-ordering tooling that parses plan text rather than ticket graph edges may sequence 225a incorrectly relative to `41e2`.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the Dependency paragraph with: 'Depends on `41e2-a0a2-2db4-4847` (CLI admission, seam child #5), which is the eval/CLI surface prerequisite designated by the parent epic (119f). The integration-seam story `2c14` and bug `8a4b` have been superseded by that epic and are closed; this story must not add a core special case to bypass the seam.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define `agreement` concretely in the Eval Contract — state its formula (e.g. 'fraction of the 12 cases where all 3 runs agree on fire/no-fire') and confirm whether `rebar criteria eval --output json` already emits this key, adding a note if it is a pre-existing field.
evidence: Plan lists required metrics as 'recall 1.0, false-accept 0.0, agreement 1.0, minimum per-case stability at least 2/3, and Cohen kappa at least 0.70' without defining `agreement`'s formula.
AC3 assertion: `assert d["recall"] == 1.0 and d["false_accept"] == 0.0 and d["agreement"] == 1.0 and d["stability_min"] >= 2/3 and d["kappa"] >= 0.70`
ABSENCE: no sentence in the plan states what `agreement` measures or whether `rebar criteria eval --output json` already outputs this key.
findings.finding: The `agreement` metric asserted in AC3's proving command (`d["agreement"] == 1.0`) is never defined or described in the Eval Contract section. The plan lists `recall`, `false-accept`, `agreement`, `minimum per-case stability`, and `Cohen kappa` as required metrics but only contextually defines recall, false-accept, kappa, and stability_min. The computation rule for `agreement` is absent: it is unclear whether it is overall percent agreement across all 36 runs, per-case agreement rate, or something else. If the existing `rebar criteria eval --output json` does not already emit an `agreement` key, the proving command throws a KeyError and the AC can never pass; if it does exist, an executor adding the output format would not know what to compute.
findings.location: Eval Contract section; AC3 proving command (`d["agreement"] == 1.0`)
scenarios: An executor adding eval output fields writes an incorrect `agreement` computation (e.g. computes it as a per-run ratio instead of a cross-run consistency score), satisfying the assertion by accident while the metric is meaningless.
If `rebar criteria eval --output json` does not emit `agreement`, the AC3 proving command raises a KeyError and the criterion can never be verified done.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the Eval Contract: 'Agreement is the fraction of the 12 eval cases where all three runs return the same fire/no-fire verdict (1.0 = perfect per-case stability across all cases); this is distinct from kappa and is emitted by `rebar criteria eval --output json` as the `agreement` key.'

No mention of what happens if _run_code_review_case is refactored as part of the dependency story 2c14-fa5f-1228-4e02 or any future kernel change
findings.finding: The eval contract couples directly to `eval_solver`'s internal `_run_code_review_case` function with no interface boundary or stability note; if that private function is renamed or refactored, the eval silently breaks with no plan-level mitigation described.
findings.location: Eval Contract section: 'criteria eval resolves the sanitized physical prompt id and reuses eval_solver's existing _run_code_review_case per-prompt arm'
scenarios: eval_solver._run_code_review_case is renamed or its signature changes during the dependency-seam repair in 2c14-fa5f-1228-4e02, causing this criterion's eval to fail at runtime with no plan-level guard
A future kernel maintainer refactors the internal function without knowing this project criterion depends on it by name

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify at minimum one observability mechanism (log line, metric counter, or trace span) for Pass-1 criterion execution success/failure so operators can monitor the pilot and debug silent failures.
evidence: 'Use routing exec: "1-TURN" and prompt execution_mode: single_turn. The finder receives the assembled diff … and returns one structured finding payload'
No mention of logging, metrics, traces, or alerting for criterion execution in any AC or scope item
'Record the live three-run eval on this ticket' is an operator-attested gate but covers only the eval harness, not production runtime observability
findings.finding: The plan adds a new live LLM invocation path (the Pass-1 criterion fires on every code_review event) but specifies no observability instrumentation — no log line, metric, or trace — for when this call succeeds, fails, times out, or returns malformed output. Operators running the pilot cannot distinguish a silently-failing criterion from a healthy one.
findings.location: Scope section / AC for criteria_routing.json activation; 'exec: 1-TURN' routing entry
scenarios: During the pilot the criterion silently times out or returns malformed JSON on every real review; operators see no findings and cannot tell whether the criterion is broken or simply found nothing
A model API outage causes the criterion to fail; without a metric/log the on-call engineer has no signal to debug the missing pilot data

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in the Eval Contract (or AC) that the eval YAML must declare `name: code_review_emits_valid_findings` (not `emits_valid_findings`) as its deterministic gate scorer, matching the code-review output schema the `_run_code_review_case` arm produces.
evidence: Plan routes under `code_review` gate: 'activates `project.review-phase-boundaries` for `code_review`'
`emits_valid_findings` in REGISTRY maps to `_schema_review_result` (checks plan-review shape with `verdict` key) — `eval_scorers.py:404`
`code_review_emits_valid_findings` maps to `_schema_code_review_findings` (checks `{findings:[...]}` without `verdict`) — `eval_scorers.py:408`
Adjacent project criterion `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml` uses `emits_valid_findings` — a plan-review scorer — which would be incorrect for a code-review criterion
Plan Eval Contract never specifies which scorer name the new YAML must use
findings.finding: The eval YAML's deterministic scorer name is unspecified, creating a risk of wiring the wrong schema validator: `emits_valid_findings` checks the plan-review `_schema_review_result` contract (which looks for a `verdict` key), while `code_review_emits_valid_findings` checks the code-review `_schema_code_review_findings` contract (which looks for a bare `{findings:[...]}` list). Since this criterion is activated under `code_review`, the eval YAML must use `code_review_emits_valid_findings`, but the plan never states this.
scenarios: Author follows portability-criterion template and writes `name: emits_valid_findings` in the new eval YAML; `validate_eval_spec(strict=True)` passes (the name is registered), but at runtime the scorer checks for a `verdict` key the code-review arm never emits, returning `ScoreResult(True, False, 'output is not a dict with verdict')` on every case and producing misleading calibration metrics.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Eval Contract section, add: 'The eval YAML's deterministic scorer must be `code_review_emits_valid_findings` (not `emits_valid_findings`) — the code-review arm returns `{findings:[...]}` without a `verdict` key, which `emits_valid_findings` / `_schema_review_result` does not recognise.'
